response:
The Terms of Service are for the MindWell Sleep Study. Here's a summary:

**Service**: This is a sleep study that uses a sleep-tracking app and a wrist sensor to collect data for 8 weeks. The study aims to understand how the app affects people with insomnia.

**Key Provisions**:
* **Participation**: By joining the study, you agree to wear the wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
* **Risks**: The study points out the risk of skin irritation from the sensor strap, but this is considered minimal.
* **Data Sharing**: De-identified data (data that doesn't include your name or personal info) may be shared with other universities. Your identifiable data (data that includes your name and contact info) will not be shared outside the research team.
* **Withdrawing**: You can withdraw from the study at any time without facing any penalty.
* **Compensation**: You'll receive $75 when you complete the study.
* **Contact**: If you have questions, you can contact the Institutional Review Board (IRB) at irb@example.edu.

**Concerns**:

* The study collects data from you for 8 weeks using a wrist sensor and weekly surveys. While the risks are minimal, there's always a chance you might experience skin irritation from the sensor strap.
* Data sharing with other universities might make you uncomfortable. However, the study assures that de-identified data will not be used to identify you.

Overall, the Terms of Service seem to be clear about the study's purpose, risks, and data sharing policies. If you have any specific concerns or questions, feel free to ask.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

**Summary of the Microsoft Services Agreement Terms of Service**

* **Service Name:** The Microsoft Services Agreement governs the relationship between you and Microsoft for its products and services.
* **Key Provisions:**
	* **Scope**: These terms apply to all Microsoft products and services, which are listed on the company's official terms page.
	* **Content and License**: When you upload content, Microsoft can use it to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
	* **Privacy**: The terms reference Microsoft's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process personal data.
	* **Dispute Resolution**: Most Microsoft services require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver. This applies unless you opt-out within 30 days of creating a new account.
	* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.
* **Notable Clauses that May be Harmful to Users:**
	* **Mandatory Arbitration**: Requiring binding arbitration with a class-action waiver can limit your options if you're unhappy with Microsoft's services.
	* **Auto-Renewal**: Some trial offers may require auto-renewal, which means you might be charged again without explicit consent.

Please note that the Summary of Updated Terms of Service mentions that some services, like Xbox, have unique terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms, but the exact details are not specified in the provided text. If you have specific concerns or questions, you can visit the Microsoft website for more information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

The Terms of Service are for the Microsoft Services Agreement. 

The main points are:

* Microsoft's products and services are covered by these Terms, which are listed on their official terms page.
* When you use these services, you agree to them, and they will be effective from 2024.
* Microsoft collects and uses your data to improve and operate its services, and to train its AI systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* To resolve disputes, you generally have to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers.
* You or Microsoft can terminate the agreement under certain conditions, which are described in the live document.
* For questions or concerns, contact Microsoft through their published legal contact information.

Some clauses may be considered harmful to users. Specifically:

* The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to sue Microsoft in court or join a class-action lawsuit.
* Microsoft collects and uses your data to train its AI systems, which may have privacy implications.
* There is no specific information about data protection, retention, or deletion, apart from cross-referencing the company's Privacy Policy.
* Users need to review Microsoft's Privacy Policy and settings to manage their data. 

Please note that these Terms of Service do not address users' rights in certain situations, such as data breach, intellectual property infringement, or death.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (2023 → 2024) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/Updates . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ .

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on OpenAI's official terms page.

* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement subject to certain conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions, see OpenAI's published legal contact information.

**Clauses to Consider:**

* **Dispute Resolution (especially the arbitration requirement)**: Binding arbitration means you'll have to settle disputes outside of court. While this can be faster and more cost-effective, you may feel it limits your ability to seek justice.
* **Class-Action Waivers**: These clauses prevent you from joining a group lawsuit against OpenAI. You should weigh whether this is a concern for you.
* **Termination**: Understand the conditions that apply to either party terminating the agreement. Review the live document for more information.

Keep in mind that these clauses are standard in many contracts, and you should review them carefully. If you have concerns or questions about specific provisions, you should reach out to OpenAI's legal contact team.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .

* **Scope**: These terms apply to OpenAI's business and API services, as described on the company's official terms page.

None explicitly stated as such, however:

* The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver may be seen as limiting user recourse in case of disputes.

* The 30-day opt-out window for new accounts might not give users sufficient time to review and consider their options.

**Additional Information:**

* The Terms of Service require users to review OpenAI's Privacy Policy, which is not included in these terms.
* Contact information for questions about these terms can be found at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/.
* The previous version of the Terms of Service is available for reference at the specified URL.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

These Terms of Service govern the Anthropic Consumer Terms of Service, which is the updated version, effective 2025. This agreement outlines the relationship between you (the user) and Anthropic.

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**1. What the Terms Cover**: These Terms apply to your relationship with Anthropic and to the products and services described on the company's official terms page. This means if you use or interact with any of Anthropic's products, you agree to these Terms.

**2. Clarification on Scope**: Anthropic clarified the scope of these Terms to include **Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps**.

**3. Acceptable Use Policy**: You agree to a set of rules on how to use Anthropic's products, as outlined in the Acceptable Use Policy.

**4. Content and Licensing**: 
- Anthropic uses user-submitted content to operate and improve its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means they process and use the content you submit.
- This Term doesn't explicitly explain what "applicable law" means, but it could be relevant for users to ask about this in case of a dispute.

**5. Privacy**: Anthropic uses a separate Privacy Policy to outline how your data is collected and processed. The key takeaway is that they collect specific categories of personal data and use it for these purposes.

**6. Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with Anthropic, most of the Terms require **binding arbitration** instead of a court proceeding. This is a private dispute process instead of a court process. Additionally, **class-action waivers**, which prevent groups from filing joint claims, are included.

**7. Opt-out Period**: New accounts have a 30-day **opt-out window** (you can choose not to participate in binding arbitration).

**8. Termination**: Either you or Anthropic can end the agreement at any time under specific conditions outlined in the live Terms.

**9. Contact**: Find Anthropic's official contact information at the bottom of the TOS page (https://www.anthropic.com).

In terms of potential harm to the user, there are a couple of clauses to be aware of:

* **Binding Arbitration and Class-Action Waivers**: This might prevent users from joining class-action lawsuits. In the future, if there's a significant issue that many users face, they may not be able to join a group effort.

Since there is no previous version for comparison, there are no changes to highlight.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms .

**Service Overview:** The Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service (API) govern the relationship between Anthropic, the company, and its users who use the company's products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms of Service apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Anthropic, you give them the right to use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms of Service link to the company's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Both you and Anthropic agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you and the company will resolve disputes outside of court, unless you opt out within 30 days of creating an account. However, please note that Steam (Valve) users do not have to agree to mandatory arbitration.
* **Termination:** Either party may terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these Terms of Service, you can find the company's contact information at the provided URL.

**Caveats and Potential Issues:**

* **Rights to Content:** When you submit content, you grant Anthropic the right to use it, which may be concerning for users who value their intellectual property.
* **Arbitration:** The mandatory arbitration clause (especially with a 30-day opt-out window) can be seen as limiting your options for resolving disputes.
* **Termination:** While either party can terminate the agreement, the conditions for termination are not explicitly stated in the provided text, so users should be aware that terms and conditions can change.

Please note that these points are based on the provided text, and it is essential to read the entire document for a comprehensive understanding of the Terms of Service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

**Service Name:** Meta (formerly Facebook) Terms of Service, effective from 2025.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms apply to all Meta products and services, which are listed on the official terms page.
2. **Using the Service**: By using Meta products, you're agreeing to these terms and other applicable policies.
3. **Your Content**: You retain ownership of your content, but Meta can use it to improve services, train its AI, and ensure safety, depending on your settings and applicable laws.
4. **Privacy**: The terms reference Meta's separate **Privacy Policy**, which explains how Meta collects and processes your personal data.
5. **Disputes**: Most of these terms require **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with class-action waivers. This means you can't represent a group in a lawsuit against Meta; you only get individual compensation.
6. **Termination**: Either you or Meta can end the agreement under certain conditions.
7. **Contact**: For questions, see Meta's published contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration**: This means you might have to resolve disputes outside of court, which can be more restrictive and less transparent than a public trial. Additionally, class-action waivers limit your ability to participate in group lawsuits.
* **Binding Arbitration**: This could lead to less favorable outcomes for you if you're involved in a dispute with Meta, as decisions might be made without a public trial.
* **Data collection and usage**: While Meta provides a privacy policy, it describes how data is collected and processed. Users should review the policy to understand how their data might be used.

Please note that these terms are subject to change, and you should familiarize yourself with them. These concerns highlight the importance of carefully reading the agreement and staying informed about any updates.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

The service is called Instagram, and these are its Terms of Service. Here's a summary:

**What Instagram Does with Your Content**

When you post on Instagram, you're granting Instagram a non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, distribute, and modify that content. This means they can use your photos, videos, and other posts to operate, improve, and even train their artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems.

**Your Personal Data**

Instagram collects personal data about you, as outlined in its Privacy Policy. The current Privacy Policy isn't provided here, but typically it explains how your data is used and processed. 

**Communication Disputes**

If you have a dispute with Instagram, you may be required to use binding arbitration instead of taking the issue to court. This means you agree to let a private dispute resolution process decide your case, rather than having it heard in a public court. Some countries have laws that may affect this provision.

**Terminating the Agreement**

Either you or Instagram can end the agreement at any time, but the terms of this termination are available in the live document.

**Where to Ask Questions**

If you have questions about the Terms of Service, Instagram encourages you to visit its Customer Support page at https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870.

Some potential points of concern for users:

* The fact that Instagram has a license to modify your content without your consent might make some users uneasy.
* The use of AI and ML systems might worry people who don't know how their data is used.
* The provision for binding arbitration might be considered unfair or one-sided to users.
 
Remember, binding arbitration has class action waivers, meaning you won't be able to join a larger group lawsuit.

This is a plain-English overview, and I recommend reading the Terms of Service document (linked at the support page) to get the most accurate and up-to-date information.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

**Service Name**
X Terms of Service, which governs the relationship between X (Twitter) and its users, as well as the rules and guidelines that apply to X's products and services.

**Key Provisions**

* **License to Use Your Content** (Clause 3): When you post content on X, you grant X a royalty-free, worldwide license to use that content for training their machine-learning and generative-AI models. * **Dispute Resolution** (Clause 5): If you have a dispute with X, you'll need to agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with class-action waivers. This means you won't be able to join a lawsuit against X with other users who may have similar complaints.
* **Termination** (Clause 6): Either X or you can terminate the agreement at any time, but the exact conditions for termination are not specified.

**Harmful Clauses**
* **License to Use Your Content** (Clause 3): Some users may be concerned about granting X a royalty-free, worldwide license to use their content. This could potentially allow X to use their posts for commercial purposes without their explicit consent.
* **Dispute Resolution** (Clause 5): Requiring binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit users' ability to seek redress for any issues they have with X.
* **Termination** (Clause 6): The lack of specific conditions for termination may leave users unclear about their rights or obligations in the event of termination.

It's essential to carefully review the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy to understand X's rules and guidelines, as well as your rights and obligations as a user. If you have concerns or questions, you can contact X using the contact information provided on their website.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

This is the TikTok Terms of Service (US). According to the document, these terms govern your relationship with TikTok and apply to the company's products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Usage and Content**: You agree to use TikTok's products and services responsibly and in accordance with the company's official policy. The company can collect and use your content, such as photos and videos, to improve its services and train its AI/ML systems, as long as you've set your preferences and applicable law permits.
* **Privacy**: The terms refer to the company's separate Privacy Policy, which explains how the company collects and processes personal data. (Personal data refers to information about you that can be used to identify you, such as your name, email address, or location.)
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have an issue with TikTok, you'll need to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). This means that you or the company can't take each other to court to resolve disputes, and any disputes will be resolved through a neutral third-party arbitration process. There is a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but after that window closes, you'll be subject to binding arbitration.
* **Termination**: Either you or TikTok can end this agreement if the other party breaches the terms. The live document will outline the conditions for termination.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Usage of Content**: The terms allow TikTok to use your content for free, including for training its AI/ML systems, although you can limit how your content is used. 
* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement for binding arbitration, which can be more expensive and less accessible than traditional court proceedings, may be a concern for some users.

**Important Contacts:**

* For questions about these terms, you can view the published legal contact information on TikTok's website at the new Terms of Service URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en

**Other Notes:**

* The terms now mention generative-AI specific rules, such as using AI output ‘as-is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, and the prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

**Service Name:** Adobe General Terms of Use

**What these terms cover:** These terms govern your relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services listed on Adobe's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** Adobe can use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, but only as per your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Adobe's Privacy Policy (which isn't included in these terms) explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. Keep an eye on this separate document.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You may be required to go to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) for disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions listed in the live document.
* **Communication:** For questions about these terms, look at Adobe's published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Access to User Content:** Adobe can access your user content via automated and manual methods to improve their services and software (clauses 1 and 3).
* **Training AI/ML Models:** Adobe can train their AI/ML systems with user-submitted content, but they claim to not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content (clause 3).
* **Binding Arbitration:** You may be required to go to binding arbitration for disputes, which might not be a suitable option for all users (clause 5).

Keep in mind that the terms aim to clarify existing language in response to user feedback.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

**Service Name: LinkedIn User Agreement**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you and LinkedIn, which governs how you use LinkedIn's products and services. Key provisions include:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to your use of LinkedIn's products and services, as described on the official terms page.
* **Content and License**: You grant LinkedIn a license to use your submitted content to operate and improve its services. However, LinkedIn must respect your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: LinkedIn's published Privacy Policy explains what categories of personal data are collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most terms require you to resolve disputes through binding arbitration instead of going to court. Arbitration is a private dispute process where a third-party decides the outcome. You have a 30-day window to opt out when creating a new account.

Clauses that may be harmful to you include:

* **Binding Arbitration**: This means you give up the right to go to court to resolve disputes. Additionally, you will not be able to join a class-action lawsuit. Please note that this is not unique to LinkedIn and has become industry standard.
* **Loss of rights in dispute resolution**: If you lose in arbitration, you may be bound by the decision and subject to the terms of the arbitration award.

We recommend you read the full terms, especially the sections on **Dispute Resolution** and **TERMINATION**, to understand the complete scope of your relationship with LinkedIn.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by LinkedIn to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/previous-user-agreement .

**Service Name:** GitHub Terms of Service (Effective 2026)

**Summary:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with GitHub, a platform for developers to collaborate and share code. They outline how GitHub uses and shares your data, how you can use the service, and what happens if you or GitHub chooses to terminate the agreement.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to GitHub's products and services listed on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: GitHub uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is processed in accordance with GitHub's published Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes are resolved through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement with conditions described in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Sharing Data with Affiliates**: Your personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development. This could potentially lead to increased data collection and usage.
* **Class-Action Waivers**: Binding arbitration with class-action waivers might limit your ability to join group lawsuits, potentially reducing the impact of legal action against GitHub.
* **Limited Opt-Out Options**: The 30-day opt-out window for new accounts might not be sufficient, leaving users without a clear option to avoid arbitration.

Keep in mind that these Terms are subject to change, and it's essential to review the live document for the most up-to-date information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

**Netflix Terms of Use Summary**

Netflix is the service offered under these Terms of Service. The key provisions are:

* **Relationship with Netflix**: These terms govern your relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services offered on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Netflix uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and the law.
* **Privacy**: The terms cross-reference Netflix's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, except Valve/Steam (in this dataset only). You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement according to the conditions described in the live document.

**Provisions that may be harmful to the user:**

* The **dispute resolution** requirement may seem restrictive, as it prefers private arbitration and class-action waivers. This means users may have limited options to join a class-action lawsuit if there's a massive issue with the service.
* The **termination** clause is broad and subject to specific conditions, which might be hard to find or understand. Users should review the live document carefully to understand when and how they or Netflix can end the agreement.
* **Content and license** provisions could raise concerns if users don't understand how their submitted content is used or shared. Be aware of how your content contributes to Netflix's AI/ML systems.

Keep in mind that these provisions are subject to the company's published Privacy Policy and terms may change over time.

To have a deeper understanding, it's recommended to review Netflix's published Privacy Policy (cross-referenced in these terms) and the live document for the conditions of termination.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with PayPal's services. The key provisions can be summarized as follows:

**Service Name:** PayPal User Agreement

**SCOPE (Clause 1):** These terms apply to the products and services described on PayPal's official terms page.

**CONTENT AND LICENSE (Clause 3):** PayPal can use content you submit to improve their services, including AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. 

**PRIVACY (Clause 4):** PayPal's Privacy Policy sets out what personal data they collect and how they process it. You should review the Privacy Policy for more information.

**DISPUTE RESOLUTION (Clause 5):** You're required to use binding arbitration for disputes with PayPal, with some exceptions. This means you give up your right to go to court, and your claim can't be in a group or class action lawsuit. 

**Important Notes:**

* You should review the Privacy Policy for information on what data PayPal collects and how it is used.
* The requirement for binding arbitration may limit your options in resolving disputes with PayPal.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* The binding arbitration requirement (Clause 5) gives up your right to go to court and may limit your access to certain dispute resolution options.
* Clause 3 allows PayPal to use your content to improve their services, which could raise data protection concerns.

**Key Contacts:**

* For questions about these terms, visit PayPal's published legal contact information at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

**Overview**
These Terms govern your relationship with eBay and apply to using their products and services. They update and replace a previous version, effective 2024.

**Key Provisions**

* **Scope**: These Terms cover your use of eBay's products and services, as described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: You agree that eBay can use content you submit to improve and train their AI systems, following your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The Terms reference eBay's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You may be required to resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party may terminate the agreement following conditions described in the document.
* **Contact**: You can reach out to eBay for questions about these Terms through their published legal contact information.

**Potential concerns for users**

* **Mandatory arbitration**: You may be required to resolve disputes through a private arbitration process that waives your right to join class-action lawsuits. This means you may not be able to seek collective damages or join a group lawsuit with others who were affected similarly.
* **Scope of data collection**: The Terms reference eBay's Privacy Policy, which controls what data is collected and processed. Be sure to read and understand the policy to know what's happening with your personal data.

Remember to review eBay's published Privacy Policy and seek guidance if you have questions about these Terms or any specific clause.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

service_name: Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions
response:
These are the **Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions**, effective 2024.

Here's a plain-language summary:

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms govern your relationship with Apple and cover its products and services, such as Apple Music and the App Store.
* Apple may use your user-submitted content to improve its AI systems, but only subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* Apple's **Privacy Policy** explains which personal data it collects and how it's processed.
* If you have a dispute with Apple, you'll need to go through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court). You can opt out within 30 days of creating your Apple account.
* Either you or Apple can **terminate** the agreement at any time, subject to certain conditions.

**Harmful Clauses to Pay Attention To:**

* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers**: This means you can't join a group lawsuit against Apple even if many others have the same issue. You can opt out within 30 days, but after that, this clause applies.

**Other Important Points:**

* Apple can change or remove its services at any time.
* You're responsible for your own content and any interactions on Apple's services.
* Note that Family Sharing and Subscriptions have been revised in these updated terms.

Remember that you can review the complete **Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions** and Apple's published **Privacy Policy** for more details.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

**Service Name:** iCloud Terms and Conditions

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services listed on their official terms page.
2. **Content and License:** Apple uses your submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. (This means Apple might use your content for their own research and development, but with some limitations.)
3. **Privacy:** The Privacy Policy sets out how Apple collects and processes your personal data. (Details can be found in Apple's separate Privacy Policy document.)
4. **Dispute Resolution:** The updated terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers for most cases. New accounts have a 30-day opt-out window, but only for this provision.
5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the current document.

**Provisions to Consider Cautiously:**

* **Data Protection:** Apple mentions end-to-end encryption with Advanced Data Protection but only under specific circumstances. The clause is too vague to confirm if this feature is enabled by default.
* **Access to Stored Content:** Apple may access your content for legal or safety reasons.
* **Data Use for AI/ML Training:** Although the clause specifies subject to your settings and applicable law, there's no explicit guarantee that Apple will not collect and use your data without your knowledge.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to participate in group lawsuits or seek compensation in certain situations.
* **Notice and Access:** Apple's 30-day opt-out window applies to the arbitration process, but there's no clarity on other potential notice periods or access limits for account holders.
* **Termination Conditions:** The clause is not entirely transparent, making it difficult to determine under what conditions Apple or you can opt-out.

**Important Caveats:**

* Apple has separate Terms of Service for other services, such as Apple Arcade or Apple News, which might have different requirements and limitations.
* Apple's Privacy Policy, referenced in the terms, contains detailed information about data collection and processing.



These points address the most noticeable parts of the service and identify potential gotchas. Users, however, should still review these Terms of Service thoroughly, paying attention to specific provisions and any updates to stay best informed.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service

**Summary:**

The Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service govern your relationship with the company that operates the Stack Overflow platform. These terms outline how you can use the platform, what happens to your content, how data is collected and used, and what to expect in case of disagreements.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all the products and services provided by Stack Overflow.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Stack Overflow, you grant the company a license to use it to operate, improve, and train the company's AI and machine learning (ML) systems. However, you have settings that allow you to control how your content is used.
* **Privacy:** Stack Overflow collects personal data, and you can find more information about this in the company's published Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court), which means you give up your right to a court trial. There is a **30-day opt-out window for new accounts**, but the details are not specified in the terms.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement, subject to the conditions outlined in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* The terms may be **harmful** if you don't carefully review the dispute resolution clause, as it requires **binding arbitration**.
* The terms also mention **bulk extraction for AI training** without a commercial agreement, but this seems to be a restriction rather than a concern.
* While the terms reference a **Privacy Policy**, it's essential to review this document in detail to understand what data is collected and how it's used.

Please remember that these terms are subject to change, and you should always review the latest version before using the Stack Overflow platform.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

**Service Name: 23andMe Terms of Service**

The 23andMe Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and the company when you use their products and services. These terms aim to explain how your data is used, how disputes are handled, and under what conditions you can terminate the agreement.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services described on 23andMe's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: 23andMe uses your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The Privacy Policy sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed. (The Privacy Policy is not included in these Terms of Service.)
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes are resolved through binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This means that you'll settle disputes outside of court and won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit if others have similar claims.
* **Termination**: Either party may terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, see 23andMe's published legal contact information.

**Flags for Harmful Clauses:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration**: 23andMe added a mandatory-arbitration clause after the October 2023 data breach. This means that if you don't opt out within 30 days, you'll be required to settle any breach-related claims through arbitration. It's essential to review and opt out if you're not comfortable with this provision.
* **Class-Action Waivers**: The mandatory-arbitration clause also includes class-action waivers, which limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit if others have similar claims.
* **Shortened Dispute-Notice Window**: The dispute-notice window has been shortened, which might affect your ability to file a complaint or dispute a decision.
* **Increased Risk with Mandatory Arbitration**: Binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) can be less favorable to users, as they may not have the same rights and protections as in a courtroom.

Please carefully review these terms to ensure you understand the agreement and any potential risks or limitations.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

- **Scope:** These terms apply to your use of Roblox's products and services.

4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . **Service Name:** Epic Games Terms of Service

**Overview:** These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you, the user, and Epic Games, Inc. They apply to all products and services described on the company's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope and Changes:** These Terms of Service govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and can be updated at any time. This 2024 version is different from the 2023 version in several key ways, including changes to content provisions, creator-payout rules, and dispute-resolution sections.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content, such as images or videos, to Epic Games, they can use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems (computer learning) as long as you have allowed them to do so according to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** This document cross-references Epic Games' published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes must be resolved through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers (meaning you can't join group lawsuits)**. However, new accounts have a 30-day window to opt-out of this requirement.
* **Termination:** Both parties can terminate the agreement, but the terms describe the necessary conditions for doing so.

**Flags:**

* **Potential harm:** The inclusion of **binding arbitration and class-action waivers** may limit your ability to resolve disputes through the court system or join group lawsuits against Epic Games. This could make it harder to hold the company accountable for their actions.
* **Limitations on control:** By allowing Epic Games to use your submitted content for their AI/ML systems, you may be giving up some control over how your content is used.

**Important Contact Information:** If you have questions about these Terms of Service, you can find Epic Games' published legal contact information on their website at the TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Airbnb Terms of Service**

These terms govern your relationship with Airbnb and cover the use of the company's products and services as listed on its official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services provided by Airbnb.
* **Content and License**: You grant Airbnb permission to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is governed by Airbnb's separate Privacy Policy, which details the categories of data collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You are required to use binding arbitration for disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you'll have a private dispute process instead of going to court.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement according to the conditions outlined in the document.

**Flagged Provisions that May be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration**: You may be required to use arbitration instead of the court system, which can be a more expensive and less favorable process for users.
* **Class-Action Waivers**: By opting for arbitration, you may also be giving up your right to join class-action lawsuits, which can be beneficial for users.
* **Termination Conditions**: The document mentions termination conditions, but these are not explicitly defined, which may leave users uncertain about when the agreement can be terminated.

**Other Notes:**

* **Updated Version Added**: The newest version of the terms was added in 2024, replacing the 2023 version. The 2024 update included new experience terms, revised cancellation and refund policies, and updated arbitration provisions.
* **Contact Information**: For questions about these terms, you can refer to Airbnb's published legal contact information at https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908.

Please note that this summary is for informational purposes only and not intended as a substitute for seeking legal advice.
